title: Equations and Inequalities
kicker: Cambridge Lower Secondary · Mathematics 0862 · Stage 8 · Algebra
summary: Turn word problems into equations, solve equations with brackets, fractions and the unknown on both sides, and use inequalities and number lines to show open and closed intervals.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Write a situation described in words as an equation, write an equation as a situation in words, and solve it. The equations can have whole-number or fraction coefficients, and the unknown can be on one side or on both sides. [8Ae.06]

Understand that a letter can stand for a whole range of numbers (an interval), shown with inequality symbols such as x > 3 or −2 < x ≤ 5 (one or two end values), and show open and closed ends on a number line. [8Ae.07]

blocks.text: An **equation** is a statement that two things are equal, such as 4x + 7 = 31. Solving it means finding the value of the letter that makes the statement true. In Stage 8 you solve harder equations — with brackets, with fractions and with the letter on **both** sides — and you turn word problems into equations yourself. You also meet **inequalities**: a letter that stands for a whole range of numbers, like all the numbers between −2 and 3. Both ideas are used again and again in Stage 9 and in the Checkpoint test, so learn the methods carefully.
1. Key words

items: equation
معادلة — two expressions joined by an = sign, e.g. 3x + 5 = 20
unknown
المجهول — the letter whose value you must find
solve / solution
يحل / الحل — find the value that makes the equation true, e.g. x = 5
inverse operation
العملية العكسية — the operation that undoes another: + undoes −, × undoes ÷
coefficient
المعامل — the number multiplying a letter: in 7x it is 7; in x/4 it is 1/4
expand
يفك الأقواس — multiply out a bracket: 3(x − 4) = 3x − 12
substitute
يعوض — put a number in place of the letter to check
inequality
متباينة — a statement using <, >, ≤ or ≥
interval
فترة — all the numbers between two end values
open / closed end
طرف مفتوح / مغلق — the end value is NOT included (○) / IS included (●)
integer
عدد صحيح — a whole number: … −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 …

blocks.text: 2. Expression, formula or equation?
Letters are used in three different ways, and it helps to know which one you are looking at.

rows: No = sign. x can be any number; you can simplify or evaluate it, but not solve it.
A rule connecting quantities. Each letter stands for a real quantity (perimeter, length, width).
True only for a particular value of x (here x = 6). You solve it.

blocks.text: 3. The balance method

Think of an equation as a pair of balanced scales. The two sides weigh the same. If you add, subtract, multiply or divide on **one** side, you must do exactly the same to the **other** side, or the scales stop balancing. Your aim is to get the letter on its own on one side.

blocks.text: **Method for solving any linear equation**

items: **Simplify each side**: expand any brackets and collect like terms.
**Letter on both sides?** Subtract the smaller letter term from both sides, so the letter is on one side only.
**Undo + or −** by doing the inverse to both sides.
**Undo × or ÷** by doing the inverse to both sides.
**Check**: substitute your answer into the ORIGINAL equation. Both sides must give the same number.

blocks.text: Example: 2x + 3 = 11 → subtract 3 from both sides: 2x = 8 → divide both sides by 2: **x = 4**. Check: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11 ✓. Write one step per line with the = signs underneath each other — it is clearer, and examiners can give you method marks even if you slip later.
4. Brackets, negative numbers and fraction answers

rows: Divide both sides by 3 first: x − 4 = 5 → add 4

blocks.text: Answers do not have to be positive whole numbers. A solution can be negative (x = −2) or a fraction (x = 5/2). Give a fraction answer in its simplest form, or as an exact decimal. Do not round 1/3 to 0.3 — that is not exact.
5. Equations with fractional coefficients

A **fractional coefficient** means the letter is multiplied by a fraction, for example (2/3)x, or divided by a number, for example x/5 (which is the same as (1/5)x). To clear the fraction, **multiply both sides by the denominator**.

blocks.title: The fraction line is a bracket
blocks.text: In (x + 7)/3 the whole of x + 7 is divided by 3. So you cannot subtract the 7 first. Multiply both sides by 3 first, which removes the fraction and leaves x + 7 = 12.
6. The unknown on both sides
When the letter appears on both sides, first remove the letter from one side. A good habit is to subtract the **smaller** letter term, so the letter term that is left is positive.

rows: Add 2x (−2x is smaller than 3x): 7 = 5x − 8 → add 8: 15 = 5x → x = 3
Multiply every term by 2: x + 10 = 4x − 2 → subtract x: 10 = 3x − 2 → 12 = 3x → x = 4

blocks.text: Notice that it does not matter if the letter ends up on the right: 15 = 5x is just as good as 5x = 15. The answer is still x = 3.
7. From words to equations — and back again
Many Checkpoint questions describe a situation in words. You must write the equation yourself.

items: Choose a letter for the unknown and say what it stands for (e.g. "Let p be the price of one pen in dollars").
Write each quantity in the problem as an expression in that letter.
Find the two things that are equal and join them with = to make the equation.
Solve the equation.
Answer the question that was asked, in words, with units — and check it makes sense in the story.

rows: the sum of n and 4, then multiplied by 3
I think of a number, multiply it by 4 and subtract 7. The answer is 25.
Three times a number is equal to the number plus 18.

blocks.text: **Going the other way.** You may be asked to write a story for an equation. For 2x + 15 = 60 you could write: "A book costs x dollars. Two books and a bag costing $15 cost $60 altogether." Any story is fine as long as every part of the equation is explained: 2x is two books, + 15 is the bag, = 60 is the total.
8. Inequalities and intervals
Sometimes a letter stands for **many** values, not just one. "The temperature was above 2 °C" does not give one number — it gives a whole range. We write this with an **inequality**: t > 2.

headers: End value on a number line
rows: x is less than or equal to 4
at most, no more than, maximum
x is greater than or equal to 4
at least, no less than, minimum

blocks.caption: Four intervals. An open circle (○) means that end value is not included; a filled circle (●) means it is included. An arrow means the interval goes on for ever.

blocks.text: A **two-term** inequality such as **−2 < x ≤ 3** gives both ends of the interval. Read it from the middle outwards: "x is greater than −2 **and** less than or equal to 3". The smaller number is always on the left. On the number line it is a line segment between −2 and 3, with an open circle at −2 and a filled circle at 3.

items: **Closed interval** — both ends included, e.g. −3 ≤ x ≤ 1 (two filled circles).
**Open interval** — neither end included, e.g. −1 < x < 4 (two open circles).
One end open and one closed, e.g. −2 < x ≤ 3.

x can be **any** number in the interval — 2.7, 1/2, −1.99 — not only whole numbers. If the question says "x is an integer", list only the whole numbers: for −2 < x ≤ 3 they are −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 (five integers; −2 is not included).
Real life: "Children aged at least 8 and under 14 can join the club" → 8 ≤ a < 14.

blocks.text: 9. Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Solve 5(x − 3) = 2x + 9. Show your working. [3]
**Answer: x = 8.** Common mistake: expanding 5(x − 3) as 5x − 3. The 5 multiplies **both** terms in the bracket.
**Worked example 2** — Solve (2x + 5)/3 = 9. [2]

items: Multiply both sides by 3: 2x + 5 = 27.
Subtract 5: 2x = 22.
Divide by 2: **x = 11**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: writing 2x/3 + 5 = 9. The 5 is also divided by 3, so clear the fraction first.
**Worked example 3** — Solve (1/3)x + 4 = x − 6. [3]

items: Multiply every term on both sides by 3: x + 12 = 3x − 18.
Subtract x from both sides: 12 = 2x − 18.
Divide by 2: **x = 15**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: multiplying only the fraction term by 3 and forgetting the other terms. **Every** term must be multiplied.

**Worked example 4** — The length of a rectangle is (2x + 3) cm and its width is (x − 1) cm. The perimeter is 40 cm. (a) Write an equation in x. [1] (b) Solve it. [2] (c) Find the length of the rectangle. [1]

rows: Let Mona's age now be m years. Then Omar is 3m.
Mona is 8 years old (Omar is 24). In 8 years: 32 and 16, and 32 = 2 × 16 ✓

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Doing something to one side only. Every step must be done to **both** sides (and to every term on a side).
Expanding brackets wrongly: 3(x − 4) is 3x − 12, not 3x − 4. Watch the signs: −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10.
Sign slips when removing a letter term: from 5x = 2x + 18, subtracting 2x gives 3x = 18 (not 7x).
With (2x + 5)/3, subtracting the 5 before multiplying by 3. Clear the fraction first.
Writing "5 less than n" as 5 − n. It is n − 5.
Leaving answers like 12/3 (simplify to 4) or rounding 1/3 to 0.3 (give the exact fraction).
Mixing up open and closed circles, or writing the smaller number on the right (3 < x < −2 is wrong; write −2 < x < 3).
Including an end value that is not allowed when listing integers, e.g. listing −2 for −2 < x ≤ 3.
Finding x but not answering the question (e.g. the question asked for the length or the age of the other person).

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Solve …" with [2] or [3] marks: show every line. Marks are usually given for correct steps, such as a correct expansion or a correct rearrangement, as well as the answer.
"Write an equation and solve it to find …": define your letter, write the equation, solve, then answer the question in words.
"Ahmed says the solution is x = 4. Is he correct? Explain." Substitute 4 into both sides and show they are not equal (or solve and compare).
"Draw a ring around the inequality shown on the number line" or "Show −1 ≤ x < 3 on the number line": check each end — open or filled circle.
"x is an integer. Write down all the possible values of x": look carefully at < and ≤ at each end.
Always check your solution by substituting — it takes 20 seconds and catches most mistakes.

blocks.title: المتباينات بالعربي
items: الدائرة الفاضية ○ يعني الرقم ده مش داخل (< أو >). الدائرة المليانة ● يعني الرقم داخل (≤ أو ≥).
−2 < x ≤ 3 معناها: x أكبر من −2 وأصغر من أو يساوي 3. الرقم الصغير دايمًا على الشمال.
"at least" يعني ≥ (على الأقل)، و"at most" يعني ≤ (على الأكثر).

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Equations and inequalities — practice quiz
blocks.intro: 14 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. No calculator. Use paper for your working, then type your answer. Mark the "show" and "explain" questions yourself using the mark scheme.

questions.e: Add 7 to both sides: 4x = 28. Divide by 4: x = 7. Check: 4 × 7 − 7 = 21 ✓
Expand: 3x + 15 = 12. Subtract 15: 3x = −3. Divide by 3: x = −1. (Or divide by 3 first: x + 5 = 4, so x = −1.) Check: 3 × 4 = 12 ✓
Subtract 3x: 5x + 5 = 30. Subtract 5: 5x = 25. Divide by 5: x = 5. Check: 45 = 45 ✓
Add 2x to both sides: 11 = 6x − 13. Add 13: 24 = 6x. Divide by 6: x = 4. Check: 11 − 8 = 3 and 16 − 13 = 3 ✓
Subtract 3: (2/5)x = 8. Multiply by 5: 2x = 40. Divide by 2: x = 20. Check: (2/5) × 20 + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11 ✓

questions.q: Solve 6x − 4 = 2x + 6. Give your answer as a fraction or a decimal.
questions.e: Subtract 2x: 4x − 4 = 6. Add 4: 4x = 10. Divide by 4: x = 10/4 = 5/2 = 2.5. Check: 15 − 4 = 11 and 5 + 6 = 11 ✓

questions.q: I think of a number, n. I subtract 4 from it, then I multiply the result by 3. The answer is 27. Which equation is correct?
questions.e: Subtracting 4 first gives n − 4; multiplying the RESULT by 3 needs a bracket: 3(n − 4) = 27. (Solving: n − 4 = 9, so n = 13.) 3n − 4 would mean multiply first, then subtract.

questions.p: A pen costs $x. A notebook costs $3 more than a pen. Hana buys 4 pens and 2 notebooks. She pays $30 altogether.
questions.ms: 1 mark: notebook = x + 3 and total written as 4x + 2(x + 3) (= 30) oe. 1 mark: correct expansion 4x + 2x + 6 = 30, leading to 6x + 6 = 30. Do not accept just writing 6x + 6 = 30 with no working.
questions.e: A notebook costs x + 3 dollars. 4 pens cost 4x; 2 notebooks cost 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6. Total: 4x + 2x + 6 = 6x + 6, and this equals 30, so 6x + 6 = 30.

questions.p: A pen costs $x. A notebook costs $3 more than a pen. Hana buys 4 pens and 2 notebooks. She pays $30 altogether.
questions.q: (b) Work out the cost of one notebook, in dollars.
questions.e: 6x + 6 = 30 → 6x = 24 → x = 4, so a pen costs $4. A notebook costs 4 + 3 = $7. Check: 4 × 4 + 2 × 7 = 16 + 14 = 30 ✓

questions.q: The three angles of a triangle are x°, (2x + 10)° and (3x − 40)°. Work out the size of the largest angle.
questions.e: Angles in a triangle add up to 180°: x + 2x + 10 + 3x − 40 = 180 → 6x − 30 = 180 → 6x = 210 → x = 35. The angles are 35°, 2 × 35 + 10 = 80° and 3 × 35 − 40 = 65°. Check: 35 + 80 + 65 = 180 ✓. Largest angle = 80°.

questions.q: Which inequality is shown on this number line?
questions.img: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 66" width="480" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><line x1="12" y1="30" x2="468" y2="30" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.8"/><polygon points="8,30 16,26 16,34" fill="#0f1b33" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="472,30 464,26 464,34" fill="#0f1b33" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M30 24V36M76.7 24V36M123.3 24V36M170 24V36M216.7 24V36M263.3 24V36M310 24V36M356.7 24V36M403.3 24V36M450 24V36" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><g font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0f1b33"><text x="30" y="52">−5</text><text x="76.7" y="52">−4</text><text x="123.3" y="52">−3</text><text x="170" y="52">−2</text><text x="216.7" y="52">−1</text><text x="263.3" y="52">0</text><text x="310" y="52">1</text><text x="356.7" y="52">2</text><text x="403.3" y="52">3</text><text x="450" y="52">4</text></g><line x1="123.3" y1="16" x2="356.7" y2="16" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width="3.5"/><circle cx="123.3" cy="16" r="6" fill="#1f5fa8" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="356.7" cy="16" r="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width="2.5"/></svg>
questions.e: The circle at −3 is filled, so −3 is included (≤). The circle at 2 is open, so 2 is not included (<). The inequality is −3 ≤ x < 2.

questions.q: x is an integer and −4 < x ≤ 1. How many different values can x take?
questions.e: −4 is not included but 1 is. The integers are −3, −2, −1, 0, 1. That is 5 values.

questions.q: A museum tour is for children aged at least 6 and younger than 12. Which inequality shows the possible ages, a years?
questions.e: "At least 6" means 6 is allowed: 6 ≤ a. "Younger than 12" means 12 is not allowed: a < 12. Together: 6 ≤ a < 12.

questions.q: Karim solves 5x − 2 = 3x + 10 and says the answer is x = 4. Is Karim correct? Show how you decide.
questions.ms: 1 mark: substitutes x = 4 to get 18 and 22 (not equal), OR solves correctly to 2x = 12. 1 mark: states Karim is not correct and the solution is x = 6. Do not accept "No" with no working.
questions.e: Substitute x = 4: left side 5 × 4 − 2 = 18, right side 3 × 4 + 10 = 22. 18 ≠ 22, so Karim is not correct. Solving properly: subtract 3x: 2x − 2 = 10, add 2: 2x = 12, so x = 6 (check: 28 = 28).

blocks.title: Remember
items: Balance method: whatever you do to one side, do to the other — and to every term.
Order: expand brackets → letters on one side (remove the smaller letter term) → undo + / − → undo × / ÷ → check.
Fractions: multiply both sides (every term) by the denominator to clear them.
Word problems: define the letter, write the equation, solve, answer the question in words with units.
Inequalities: ○ = not included (< >), ● = included (≤ ≥); smaller number on the left; read "at least" as ≥ and "at most" as ≤.
